rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant stepped mass with coherent continuity across views, so gesture and hierarchy are solid. It responds to the parcel reasonably well and does not visibly collide or fragment across the four views. The road edge is acknowledged, but the public void/threshold is relatively weak: the access side is more of a sealed/oblique edge than a clearly worked street court or undercut. The silhouette is stepped, but still coherent enough to score above a generic tiered stack because the section feels capacity-bearing rather than arbitrary. Programmatically, the mass can plausibly support a neighborhood mixed-use/living brief: compact, capacity-aware, and with an upper hierarchy that does not erase the ground relation. However, the section lacks a stronger daylight/entry articulation, so section_program_fit is only moderate. The similar references support the overall strategy of compact dominant body plus stepped relief; the second reference also supports a low street-volume with a distinct vertical accent, though it is less directly relevant. No hard typology mismatch is present, so the form passes program fit.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Taller and more tower-like than the candidate; transfer the hierarchy and void logic, not the vertical proportion.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single compact dominant mass can gain urban presence through stepped relief and a carved top/side void while preserving one readable body.
